---
description: "Use when building or modifying React components, app layout, controls, styling, or accessibility."
applyTo:
  - "src/components/**"
  - "src/App.tsx"
  - "src/App.css"
  - "src/index.css"
---
# React UI Instructions

- Use function components and the existing game/settings contexts. Dispatch game actions for shared state changes; do not duplicate blackjack rules in components.
- Use Fluent UI v9 components and design tokens, following nearby component and styling patterns. Do not hard-code colors; use `tokens` in `makeStyles` or the theme's CSS variables in stylesheets, so components follow the theme mode and accent chosen in the Appearance settings.
- Appearance settings (theme mode, accent, card style, card back pattern and color) are typed keys of `SettingsState` with their allowed values in `settingOptions`. Add new presets to `src/theme/` and keep the Options panel controls to stock Fluent components.
- Preserve accessible names for interactive controls with labels or `aria-label`; retain useful tooltip relationships and keyboard-operable controls.
- There is no splash screen. Before a game, `src/components/Table.tsx` shows the selected players as floating seat chips in the queue and the dealer on its bench, and starts play with the Start game button in the dock. Do not reintroduce splash-screen visibility settings or a separate player-selection start dialog.
- The Players dialog in `src/components/PlayersDialog.tsx` is opened from the header. It creates named profiles, selects the human profile for the next game, and shows profile statistics; a roster change never touches a hand in play: it is seated through the `SetRoster` action, which the reducer ignores until the round is settled. Between hands App applies it at once; a change made during play is applied by the Next hand button (or the Options panel's Deal) before dealing. When a hand ends, the action toolbar in the dock is replaced by a primary Next hand button (styled like Start game) and a secondary Change players button; Change players opens the same dialog through `PlayersDialogContext`, which App provides.
- The Table has three seat areas. Players wait as `SeatChip`s in the queue (`.table-queue`) in turn order; the dealer waits on its bench (`.table-bench`) above the stage; the seat in control, or one the user clicked, expands on the stage (`.table-focus`) as a `PlayerContainer`. During a hand the queue is a conveyor grouped as Up next and Played, from `seatOrder` in `src/functions/round.ts`; do not derive turn order in components. On a board at least 720px wide the queue takes a third at the side chosen by the `queueSide` setting (left by default). Below that the board is one column (queue, bench, stage), chips are compact full-width rows, and the bench keeps extra vertical margin so the dealer stands apart. `useSeatFlip` animates slots (`data-seat-key`, `data-seat-role` of `queue`, `bench` or `focus`) when they change role or place; it measures layout offsets, so `.table-board` must stay a positioned ancestor of the slots. The staged seat gets visual focus only; keyboard focus stays with the dock's buttons.
- The dock (`.table-dock`) is one row along the board's bottom edge, sticky to the bottom of the window: the pot, then the game's buttons, then the activity log button. Keep it to one row at every width. Its middle shows Start game before a game, `ControlPanel` for the human (the action toolbar, or Next hand and Change players once the hand ends), and "<name> is playing" during a computer seat's turn. Game buttons belong in the dock, not in a seat; the pre-deal wager hint is the exception and stays in the human's staged seat. The toolbar collapses to icons from the `dock-actions` container query in `Table.css`.
- The pot stays at the start of the dock before, during and after a hand; do not move it around the table. `usePotMotion` slides the last pot up out of its slot and the new one in from the top when a hand or game begins, and shimmers and bounces it when it grows; the controls and dealer automation wait through `PotAnimationContext` until it finishes. With reduced motion there is no bounce and no wait.
- The page shell in `src/App.tsx` is a flex column at least as tall as the window, and the Table (`.table-shell` and `.table-board`) grows to fill the height below the header, shrinking when the activity drawer opens but never below its content. The table sits `PAGE_GUTTER` (`src/theme/layout.ts`) from the header and from the left, right and bottom edges of the page; use that one value for all four margins (the header's bottom margin and the shell's padding) so they stay equal.
- The Activity Log is a drawer that extends from the bottom edge of the Table (`Table` renders it in `.table-shell`, beneath the board, so it never covers the seat controls). The icon button at the end of the dock toggles it. Whether it is open lives in `useActivityDrawer`: the `isActivityLogVisible` setting ("Open Activity Log by default") only decides the starting state, and applies at once when changed. Keep the drawer bounded to its fixed maximum height and scroll its entries vertically when they overflow, while keeping its heading visible and preserving horizontal table scrolling. While closed it must stay `inert` and `aria-hidden`.
- `useTableToasts` owns the toast timeline and paces the activity log. Toasts are a short running feed (`TableToasts`) rendered inside the dock, which anchors it just above the dock's top edge so the notices stay beside the buttons however far a tall board is scrolled; do not move it back to the top of the board. Toasts arrive in order, `TOAST_GAP_MS` apart, and stay beside the lines already showing, newest at the bottom with older lines dimmer. Every toast gets the same schedule whatever its kind: it fades after `TOAST_LIFE_MS`, or sooner when more than `TOAST_MAX_LINES` are showing and it is the oldest, and takes `TOAST_EXIT_MS` to close up. The hook returns a change's log entries once the last toast of that change has been on screen for `TOAST_REVEAL_MS`; `ActivityLog` then slides the new rows in from above. Entries with no toast of their own wait behind the toast still due, so the log stays in order. Keep `ACTIVITY_ROW_ENTER_MS` and `ACTIVITY_DRAWER_MS` in step with `App.css`, and cover timing changes with fake timers.
- Keep the in-app rules in `src/components/RulesDialog.tsx` and the README's Rules section accurate with the reducer/domain behavior. When blackjack rules or available actions change, update both descriptions and their relevant tests.
- Preserve the responsive table and seat behavior, and respect reduced-motion preferences when adding animation.
- Keep dealer automation in `src/components/Agent.tsx`; clean up timers and other effects when dependencies change or components unmount.
- Add or update colocated React Testing Library tests for user-visible behavior and accessibility-relevant changes.
